description: Generic dropdown select component supporting typed options (string, Guid, enum, and the following numeric types — int, short, ushort, long, ulong, uint, byte, sbyte, decimal, double, float, including their nullable forms; other TValue such as bool, DateOnly, TimeOnly, DateTime, char, nint/nuint are not supported and silently fall back to default), label, placeholder, error/help text, disabled state, and manual option rendering via ChildContent. Uses native HTML <select> element with automatic value conversion. When TValue options come from the Options parameter, the round-trip is culture-invariant: both the rendered <option>/<select> value attribute and the change-event parser always use CultureInfo.InvariantCulture (e.g. decimal/double values render and parse as "1.5", never a culture-specific "1,5"), so the ambient thread culture cannot break selection. This invariance does NOT extend to ChildContent — see the ChildContent parameter for what a hand-written <option value> must contain. The bound Value is preselected regardless of whether options come from the Options parameter or from ChildContent (raw <option> children) — the component sets the <select> value attribute so the browser reflects the current selection on load.

parameters.name: Placeholder
parameters.description: Placeholder option shown when no value is selected.

parameters.name: HelpText
parameters.description: Help text shown below the select when no error is present.

parameters.name: Required
parameters.description: Marks the select as required. Shows a required marker on the label and sets aria-required on the <select> element.

parameters.name: Options
parameters.description: Typed option list. When provided, <option> elements are generated automatically. Prefer this over ChildContent.

parameters.name: ChildContent
parameters.description: Manually rendered <option> elements. Use when you need full control over option markup. The bound Value is still preselected — the component writes the <select> value attribute so the browser selects the matching <option> on load. Unlike the Options parameter, a raw <option value="@x"> renders through Blazor's own ambient-culture ToString(), NOT through this component's invariant formatting — so for a non-integer IFormattable TValue (decimal, double, float, DateTime, ...) you must write the value explicitly as value="@x.ToString(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)" (e.g. "1.5", never a culture-specific "1,5") to match what HandleChangeAsync's invariant parser accepts; plain string/Guid/enum/integer values are unaffected.

examples.title: Basic select with string options and two-way binding
Pre-selecting a value (setting initial selection)
Select with integer value type
examples.code:
<TmSelect TValue="int"
          @bind-Value="_selectedCategoryId"
          Label="Category"
          Placeholder="Select category"
          Options="@_categoryOptions" />

@code {
    private int _selectedCategoryId;

    private List<SelectOption<int>> _categoryOptions =
    [
        new(1, "Electronics"),
        new(2, "Books"),
        new(3, "Clothing"),
        new(4, "Sports")
    ];
}

examples.title: Select with decimal value type (culture-invariant round-trip)
Select with Guid value type
examples.code:
<TmSelect TValue="Guid"
          @bind-Value="_selectedTenantId"
          Label="Tenant"
          Placeholder="Select tenant"
          Options="@_tenantOptions" />

@code {
    private Guid _selectedTenantId;
    private List<SelectOption<Guid>> _tenantOptions = [];

    protected override void OnInitialized()
    {
        _tenantOptions =
        [
            new(Guid.Parse("a1b2c3d4-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"), "Tenant Alpha"),
            new(Guid.Parse("a1b2c3d4-0000-0000-0000-000000000002"), "Tenant Beta")
        ];
    }
}

examples.title: Select with disabled options
examples.code:
<TmSelect TValue="string"
          @bind-Value="_selected"
          Label="Subscription Plan"
          Options="@_planOptions" />

@code {
    private string? _selected;

    private List<SelectOption<string>> _planOptions =
    [
        new("free", "Free"),
        new("pro", "Pro"),
        new("enterprise", "Enterprise", isDisabled: true)  // User cannot select this
    ];
}

Manual option rendering via ChildContent (with preselection)
Loading options from API on page load
Programmatic value change and reacting to selection
examples.code:
<TmSelect TValue="string"
          Value="@_selected"
          ValueChanged="OnSelectionChanged"
          Label="Status"
          Options="@_statusOptions" />

<button @onclick="() => _selected = "active"">Set Active</button>
<button @onclick="() => _selected = null">Clear</button>

@code {
    private string? _selected;

    private List<SelectOption<string>> _statusOptions =
    [
        new("active", "Active"),
        new("inactive", "Inactive"),
        new("archived", "Archived")
    ];

    private async Task OnSelectionChanged(string? newValue)
    {
        _selected = newValue;
        // React to the change — e.g. reload dependent data
        Console.WriteLine($"Status changed to: {newValue}");
    }
}
